reason: Both pick the same three bundles and right pairings, but Output 2 keeps the ₹499 threshold that matches the COD-refusal cliff and adds a COD fee idea and clear test rules; Output 1 moves to ₹599 with invented take-rate assumptions that weaken the money case.
biggest_strength_1: Strong ladder logic and a clear bundle-first test order.
biggest_mistake_1: Moves free shipping to ₹599 on made-up add/pay/walk rates, ignoring that ₹499 is the COD-refusal cliff.
what_would_make_it_a_10_1: Work the threshold off real order-band data and show the COD/RTO cost of every option, not assumed rates.
biggest_strength_2: Keeps ₹499 for the right reason (COD refusal cliff and serum reorder) and adds a COD fee test with stop rules.
biggest_mistake_2: Several money figures are rough projections built on assumed 20-35% add rates, so the owner can't fully trust them.
what_would_make_it_a_10_2: Replace assumed ranges with an order-export calculation and give the bundles one clean unit-economics table.
